title: Relative Weil extension across codimension at least two
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, with fraction field $E$, and let $T$ be a nonempty open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $X\to T$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $G\to T$ be a smooth separated group scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here a group scheme consists of multiplication $G\times_TG\to G$, inverse $G\to G$ and identity $T\to G$ satisfying the associativity, identity and inverse diagrams; neither commutativity nor properness is assumed. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme and $u:V\to G$ a $T$-morphism. Assume that $V_t=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is dense in $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ for every $t\in T$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field], and that $V$ contains every $x\in X$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq1$. Then there exists a $T$-morphism $\overline u:X\to G$ with $\overline u|_V=u$. No quasi-compactness or separatedness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: First verify the base hypothesis. Write $T=\bigcup_{f\in F}D(f)$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}D$, using the principal-open basis of the Zariski topology. The ideal generated by $F$ is finitely generated because $D$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Expressing its finitely many generators as finite sums of multiples of elements of $F$ gives a finite subset $F_0\subset F$ with $(F_0)=(F)$. A prime contains $F_0$ exactly when it contains $F$, so $T=\bigcup_{f\in F_0}D(f)$. The localization map $D\to D_f$ induces an open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}D_f\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ with image $D(f)$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], so the open subscheme $D(f)$ of $T$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}D_f$ [def-weil-open-immersion]; these chart rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Thus $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, precisely the Noetherian hypothesis in [lem-sfb-relative-group-weil-extension].

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; finite-generation argument written out. Principal-open affine construction: schemes.tex, Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), and Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves (3), (6)).

proof.text: For a point $t\in T$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset D$, restriction to an open subscheme leaves the stalk unchanged [def-weil-open-immersion]. The affine stalk identification in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], applied to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}D$, gives $\mathcal O_{T,t}\cong D_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] to the given integrally closed domain $D$ and $D\setminus\mathfrak p$: this multiplicative subset excludes zero because $\mathfrak p$ is proper. Consequently every stalk of $T$ is an integrally closed domain. Together with step 1, $T$ is a normal Noetherian base in the exact sense required by the general extension theorem.

source.place: Tag 00GY, lemma-localize-normal-domain; affine stalk identification: schemes.tex, Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves (6)).

proof.text: Apply the existing general theorem [lem-sfb-relative-group-weil-extension] with $(S,Z,H,U,u)=(T,X,G,V,u)$. Steps 1 and 2 give its base hypothesis. The assumed smoothness of $X\to T$ and of the separated group $G\to T$ are exactly its morphism hypotheses. Its fibrewise density condition is the stated density of $V_t$ in $X_t$, and its codimension condition is exactly that $V$ contain all $x$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq1$. It provides a $T$-morphism $\overline u:X\to G$ restricting to $u$, as required. That theorem explicitly allows non-quasi-compact $X$ and $G$, does not require $X$ separated, and does not require connected or commutative groups, so no additional hypothesis has been introduced.
